problem.statement: Every mission pays for a separate verification swarm even though delivery already runs its own tests at integration.

hypothesis: If the independent verification swarm is retired and delivery's own integration tests are trusted, missions will finish with fewer worker invocations and less time, with no more defects escaping.
expected_benefit: Fewer worker invocations and a shorter completion time per mission.
possible_regressions: A defect that delivery's own tests do not cover would reach the review packet unverified

change.summary: Sets independent_verification to false: no verification swarm is formed and the integrated result is accepted on delivery's own combined tests.

known_regressions: 5 more defects reached an accepted result than under the incumbent
limitations: Each episode is a complete fixture mission: the runtime, worker processes, merges and tests are real, the work content is scripted.
A defect is injected into one worker's first attempt in about 50% of episodes. That rate is an assumption of this testbed; the size of any effect depends on it.
The oracle is the same protected acceptance suite the verification swarm uses, so this measures what happens when nobody runs it — not whether it is a complete specification.
8 episodes per arm: intervals are wide.
justification: Rejected: no more defects escape failed. Acceptance criteria that fail on results the mission accepted: candidate 5, incumbent 0, across 8 episodes.
